body:
KKR has agreed to acquire private capital fund administrator Gen II Fund Services from Hg, General Atlantic and other minority investors for a $5.1bn enterprise value through its Core Private Equity strategy.Gen II administers more than $2tn of private-fund capital for more than 275 investment managers. Hg and General Atlantic invested in the business in 2020, when it administered just over $375bn; Gen II has since quadrupled both revenue and EBITDA while completing four acquisitions. KKR plans to expand the business internationally, broaden its services and invest further in proprietary technology and AI. CEO and co-founder Steven Millner will remain in charge, with completion expected in 2027.

General Catalyst, Koch Equity Development and co-investors have agreed a $2bn convertible preferred investment in Axiom, the cloud and power infrastructure business being separated from Flex, at an initial enterprise value of $37.5bn. The capital will help finance Axiom’s acquisition of EPC Power and strengthen its balance sheet ahead of its planned separation as an independently listed company in the first quarter of 2027. Axiom is being positioned around power, thermal and compute infrastructure serving growing AI infrastructure demand.

TDR Capital has agreed to acquire critical infrastructure services provider OCU Group from Triton Partners after a four-year ownership period in which revenue more than quadrupled from £295m to £1.2bn. Triton backed 18 acquisitions and OCU’s expansion into Australia and New Zealand after buying the formerly regional UK utilities business in 2022. OCU now has an order book exceeding £4bn and deploys a workforce of about 5,500 across the UK, Australia, New Zealand and India.

GE HealthCare has agreed to acquire PET radiopharmaceutical manufacturer SOFIE Biosciences from Trilantic North America for $945m in cash. SOFIE operates 15 US contract-manufacturing sites with 21 cyclotrons as well as a theranostics-focused CDMO facility, giving GE HealthCare a sizeable manufacturing and distribution network for time-sensitive PET radiopharmaceuticals. The acquisition also includes US rights to Phase III pan-cancer imaging candidate FAPI-74 and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Accel-KKR has invested in rental-industry software specialist Point of Rental, adding a business serving more than 6,000 rental companies across over 80 countries to its software portfolio. Point of Rental, founded in 1982, supplies software across equipment, tool, aerial, access and event-rental markets and has operations in the US, UK, Australia and Canada. Its recent development has included AI and machine-learning capabilities built around four decades of rental-performance data.

Aurora Capital Partners has acquired Softdocs, the cloud document-management and workflow automation software business previously backed by Ridgemont Equity Partners. Softdocs provides enterprise content management and process automation to higher education, K-12 and government customers, with more than 1,000 organisations using its products globally. The transaction gives Aurora a vertical software platform exposed to continued digitisation of administrative processes across education and government.
